q: A goods clerk books a consignment at a terminal and issues the railway receipt through the terminal system, but the freight figure in the Traffic Accounts check differs from the terminal record. Which system record is the starting point for resolving the difference?

options.B: The TMS terminal record in FOIS, since freight earnings originate in FOIS/TMS

e: Goods booking, freight calculation and terminal collections are FOIS/TMS system data; an accounts objection on goods earnings is normally an objection on a FOIS entry.

q: The E-CR (Earnings Cash Remittance) details entered in IPAS do not agree with the figures appearing in FOIS for the same period. What is the correct course?

options.A: Ignore the difference because the two systems are independent
options.B: Write off the difference in IPAS
options.C: Reconcile the IPAS E-CR details with the FOIS figures and clear the difference as an internal-check item

e: E-CR details entered in IPAS are reconciled with FOIS figures; differences are a standard internal-check item.

q: A respondent railway receives an electronic transfer advice in e-Recon for work done on its behalf by another railway. The advice is in order. What must the respondent railway still do?

options.A: Nothing, because electronic advice needs no acceptance
options.B: Record its acceptance in e-Recon so that the transfer transaction is complete
options.D: Raise a fresh debit for the same amount

e: Acceptance is still necessary under e-Recon; the electronic advice does not abolish acceptance.

q: A division finds several transfer transactions lying unmatched and unaccepted in e-Recon at the close of accounts. What does e-Recon enable the division to do?

options.A: Monitor the unmatched and unaccepted items online and chase them division-wise till cleared
options.B: Automatically write them off at year end
options.C: Transfer them to the station balance sheet

e: e-Recon provides online monitoring of unmatched/unaccepted transfer transactions so outstandings can be chased division-wise.

q: Demurrage and wharfage charges shown in a goods earnings statement are disputed by the station. To verify the charges, the TIA should trace them back to:

options.D: The FOIS/TMS entries for the terminal transactions

e: Demurrage, wharfage, siding transactions and goods earnings statements all trace back to FOIS/TMS entries.

q: A passenger buys an unreserved ticket at a counter and another reserves a berth online. Which pairing of systems has generated the coaching earnings data that Traffic Accounts will check?

options.B: UTS for the unreserved ticket and PRS for the reservation

e: PRS (Passenger Reservation System) and UTS (Unreserved Ticketing System) generate the coaching earnings data checked by Traffic Accounts.

q: During a FOIS-based check, a TIA finds that the classification of a consignment in the terminal record does not match the goods tariff applied. The TIA's general check under FOIS covers:

options.A: Only staff attendance at the terminal
options.B: Only the cash balance at the terminal
options.C: Correctness of booking, classification, freight and terminal records

e: Traffic Accounts checks on FOIS data cover correctness of booking, classification, freight and terminal records.

q: Consider the following statements about e-Recon: 1. It is the electronic system for reconciliation of inter-railway transfer transactions. 2. Under e-Recon, acceptance of a transfer advice by the respondent railway is no longer necessary. 3. Unmatched and unaccepted transfer items can be monitored online. Which statements are correct?
e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is the classic trap: acceptance remains necessary under e-Recon.

q: Consider the following statements about FOIS and TMS: 1. FOIS is the Freight Operations Information System on which freight operations run. 2. TMS, the Terminal Management System, is the operating core through which goods terminals book consignments and issue railway receipts. 3. TMS handles passenger reservations. Which statements are correct?
e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Passenger reservation is the work of PRS, not TMS.

q: What is the full form of FOIS?
e: FOIS stands for Freight Operations Information System.

q: Which organisation designs and maintains most railway computer applications such as PRS, UTS and FOIS?

options.D: CRIS — Centre for Railway Information Systems

e: Most railway applications are designed and maintained by CRIS, the Railways' own IT organisation.

q: The internal data communication network (intranet) of Indian Railways is called:
e: Internal communication across the Railways runs on Railnet, the in-house intranet.

q: In the FOIS family, rake management is handled by which sub-system?
e: Related sub-systems of FOIS handle rake management through RMS, the Rake Management System.

q: Which of the following statements about UTS and PRS is NOT correct?

options.A: UTS is the Unreserved Ticketing System
options.B: PRS is the Passenger Reservation System
options.C: Both PRS and UTS generate coaching earnings data checked by Traffic Accounts
options.D: UTS is the system through which goods terminals issue railway receipts

e: Railway receipts at goods terminals are issued through TMS under FOIS, not through UTS.

q: Which of the following is NOT a function of e-Recon?

options.A: Online monitoring of unaccepted transfer advices
options.B: Booking of freight consignments at goods terminals
options.C: Keeping Transfer Railways balances clean through timely acceptance and clearance

e: Freight booking at terminals is a FOIS/TMS function; e-Recon deals only with transfer transactions between railways.

q: Which pairing is NOT correct?

options.D: E-CR details in IPAS — reconciled with the pension figures in ARPAN

e: E-CR details entered in IPAS are reconciled with the figures appearing in FOIS, not with ARPAN.

q: Assertion (A): Under e-Recon, a transfer transaction is complete only when the respondent railway accepts the advice. Reason (R): e-Recon replaced manual registers with online monitoring, but it did not abolish the requirement of acceptance.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: Acceptance remains necessary under e-Recon; online monitoring was added without abolishing acceptance, which explains A.

q: Match List I (system) with List II (function): I. FOIS a. Unreserved ticketing II. TMS b. Freight operations system III. UTS c. Terminal booking and railway receipts IV. PRS d. Passenger reservation
e: FOIS is the freight system, TMS its terminal core, UTS unreserved ticketing and PRS reservation.

q: Match List I with List II: I. e-Recon a. Designs railway IT systems II. CRIS b. Reconciliation of transfer transactions III. Railnet c. Earnings Cash Remittance details IV. E-CR d. Railways' intranet
e: e-Recon reconciles transfers, CRIS builds the systems, Railnet is the intranet and E-CR is the remittance detail reconciled with FOIS.

q: Match List I with List II: I. RMS a. Terminal Management System II. COIS b. Rake Management System III. TMS c. Coaching Operations Information System IV. FOIS d. Freight Operations Information System
e: RMS = rake management, COIS = coaching operations information, TMS = terminal management, FOIS = freight operations.

q: Match List I (check item) with List II (source record): I. Freight correctness a. PRS/UTS data II. Coaching earnings b. FOIS/TMS entries III. Demurrage and wharfage c. e-Recon advices IV. Transfer acceptance d. FOIS/TMS terminal records
e: Freight and demurrage/wharfage trace to FOIS/TMS, coaching earnings to PRS/UTS, and transfer acceptance to e-Recon advices.

q: Match List I with List II: I. Originating railway a. Records acceptance of the advice II. Respondent railway b. Raises the transfer debit/advice III. e-Recon c. Shows unmatched items online IV. IPAS d. Carries E-CR details reconciled with FOIS
e: The originator raises the advice, the respondent accepts it, e-Recon monitors unmatched items, and IPAS carries the E-CR details.

q: Match List I (traffic) with List II (system): I. Goods booking a. UTS II. Reserved tickets b. TMS III. Unreserved tickets c. PRS IV. Freight train rakes d. RMS
e: Goods booking runs on TMS, reserved tickets on PRS, unreserved tickets on UTS and rakes on RMS.

q: Match List I with List II: I. Siding transactions a. FOIS/TMS entries II. Goods earnings statements b. FOIS/TMS entries III. Terminal collections c. FOIS/TMS system data IV. Pension revision d. ARPAN
e: Siding transactions, goods earnings statements and terminal collections all rest on FOIS/TMS data; pension revision is ARPAN's field.

q: Match List I with List II: I. FOIS a. Moves the goods II. PRS/UTS b. Generate coaching earnings III. e-Recon c. Settles claims between railways IV. CRIS d. Maintains the systems
e: FOIS moves the goods, PRS/UTS generate coaching earnings, e-Recon settles inter-railway claims and CRIS maintains the systems.
